preregistration.revision_scope: pin three items that the independent review of the hosted acquisition lane (PR #56) showed the base text and R2-R4 leave open: how a retained, offline A3 evidence bundle is bound to the governing plan revision when the base plan's artifacts and evidence schemas name only the base plan (R5-V01 through R5-V03); the exact capture points of the L and H relative-growth baselines, which checkpoint_design.relative_growth_rule calls post-create while the checked A2 worker the base plan orders reused captures them at each role's first relative batch (R5-L01); and whether bounds.campaign_timeout_seconds = 2700 is a hard evidence bound or an advisory outcome gate (R5-T01). No predicate id, mapping, sequence, scientific model, bound value, checkpoint, row algorithm, page-capture rule, or acquisition gate changes. Nine evidence schemas gain required binding fields and the bundle manifest gains two timing fields and one inventory role, enumerated with old and new SHA-256 in R5-V02; plan.schema.json and dry-run-report.schema.json are unchanged
preregistration.derivation_basis: R5-V01 is derived from the immutable base plan's implementation_rebinding.worker_fail_closed_rule (every emitted document must carry the exact id and plan SHA-256), its artifacts.plan inventory entry, decision_rules, and the independent_validator_contract, all of which bind evidence to the plan by hash; a revision chain that the analyzer and validator actually implement must be bound the same way or the offline bundle is governed by text it was not evaluated under. R5-L01 is derived from checkpoint_design (the D phase precedes the first L batch in checkpoint_ids, d_growth_rule and d_regrowth_rule each add at least 128 pages, and transition_coverage and polarity_cross_check_legs require eight consecutive growing L_REL checkpoints), from implementation_rebinding.source_rule (reuse the checked A2 worker without schedule changes), from schedule_minimization_basis (no checkpoint was retuned after inspecting EXP-0042), and from the A2 worker's capture point under which the EXP-0042 design inputs that calibrate the legs were produced. R5-T01 is derived from runtime_design.campaign_headroom, which defines 2700 as the exact sum of the 1700-second worker ceiling, the 900-second fan-in ceiling, and the 100-second setup and dispatch allowance, and from bounds_sanity_basis, which requires every bound to accept its exact ceiling and reject one over. The PR #56 implementation and the review were read only to locate the gaps; no rule adopts an implementation because it is convenient. No DAO observation, holdout artifact, or A3 replica was inspected

gaps.title: governing revision hash in every evidence document and the revision chain in the closed bundle inventory
gaps.plan_gap: the base plan binds every evidence document to the base plan by plan_sha256 and inventories only plan/a3-allocation-maps.plan.json, while the analyzer, independent validator, worker, and workflow implement R2, R3, and R4. The evidence schemas carry additionalProperties false and no revision field, and R3 and R4 declare them immutable, so a retained offline bundle can state only that it was produced under the base plan. PR #56 pins R2-R4 in the worker and the fan-in diagnostics, but no schema-valid evidence document and no closed inventory entry records the governing revision
gaps.rule: Every A3 evidence document (replica observation, page index, replica artifact manifest, environment, frozen derivation candidate set, holdout structure receipt, analysis report, bundle manifest, and independent validation report) carries a required field revision_plan_sha256 whose value is the SHA-256 of the governing revision plan file. For every document produced under this revision that value is the SHA-256 of oracle/windows-dao/experiments/a3/a3-allocation-maps-r5.plan.json, which is recorded in the provenance entry, README, a3_spec.py, and the independent validator, not in any schema. The governing revision is the highest-numbered additive revision recorded before acquisition starts; a later additive revision recorded before acquisition starts replaces this value by its own hash and must restate this rule. The field is placed immediately after plan_sha256 in each schema's required list and properties. The closed evidence bundle additionally retains every revision plan file of the chain at plan/a3-allocation-maps-r2.plan.json, plan/a3-allocation-maps-r3.plan.json, plan/a3-allocation-maps-r4.plan.json, and plan/a3-allocation-maps-r5.plan.json, each inventoried in bundle-manifest.json with role revision_plan, media type application/json, and its SHA-256 equal to the hash pinned for that revision; the base plan stays at plan/a3-allocation-maps.plan.json with role plan. The worker must refuse to create a database unless every revision file of the chain hashes to its pinned value and every emitted document carries revision_plan_sha256; the producer validator must reject a bundle whose manifest, documents, or inventory lack the field, carry a value other than the governing hash, omit any of the four revision entries, or carry a revision entry whose bytes do not hash to the inventoried and pinned value; the independent validator must recompute every one of those checks from the bundle bytes and the repository-pinned hashes, and its own report carries the same field. A tamper that removes or alters any revision entry, or alters revision_plan_sha256 in any single document, must be rejected; that rejection is demonstrated by checked tests of the producer validator and the independent validator, and the reported T1-T5 tamper suite and its schema are unchanged
gaps.single_implementation: revision_plan_sha256 required after plan_sha256 in nine evidence schemas; four revision_plan inventory entries at plan/*-r2..r5.plan.json; value and hashes pinned in code, never in a schema
gaps.rationale: a schema const would make the schema hash depend on the revision hash and the revision on the schema hash, so the binding is pinned in the checked contract modules instead, exactly as plan_sha256 is today. Retaining the whole chain rather than only the governing file lets a detached consumer read every superseding rule without a repository checkout

relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.title: exact L and H relative-growth baseline capture points
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.plan_gap: checkpoint_design.relative_growth_rule says each L_REL or H_REL checkpoint is the first closed-file state after a fixed 32-row batch whose page count is at least that table's post-create baseline plus the named target, but never says when that baseline is read. All four tables are created before E0, so a literal reading captures the L and H baselines at the post-create file size. The checked A2 worker that implementation_rebinding.source_rule orders reused captures each role's baseline at the role's first relative batch, and the PR #56 A3 worker inherits that. The review ruled that the specific checkpoint rule controls the scientific threshold and that the inherited capture point is a plan divergence until preregistered
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.rule: The L baseline is the closed-file page count of the database in the state captured as D_REGROW_0128, read once, before the first L batch; it therefore equals the actual_file_pages recorded for D_REGROW_0128, which is the immediately preceding checkpoint and is followed by no operation. The H baseline is the closed-file page count of the state captured as P_ABS_16480, read once, before the first H batch; it equals the actual_file_pages recorded for P_ABS_16480. Page count means the total closed-file page count of the database file (file size divided by page_size), not the table's own pages. Target semantics: the threshold of L_REL_nnnn is the L baseline plus nnnn and the threshold of H_REL_nnnn is the H baseline plus nnnn; each such checkpoint is the first closed-file state after a fixed 32-row batch into that role whose total file page count is at least its threshold; target_overshoot_pages is the achieved count minus the threshold. The named target is thus file growth attributable to the role's insertions beyond the state in which the role first grows, not beyond the file's post-create size. The immutable base plan is not edited: this rule resolves the conflict between relative_growth_rule's phrase that table's post-create baseline and implementation_rebinding.source_rule by fixing the reading of that phrase, for the L and H roles, as the closed-file state in which the role first grows; every other word of relative_growth_rule, and d_growth_rule and d_regrowth_rule, which already name their own capture points, are read literally
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.disclosure_rule: Every L_REL and H_REL checkpoint of every replica observation records target_baseline_pages equal to the baseline defined above, target_threshold_pages equal to that baseline plus the named target, and target_overshoot_pages equal to actual_file_pages minus target_threshold_pages, at least 0. The producer validator and the independent validator must reject an observation in which, for any L_REL checkpoint, target_baseline_pages differs from the actual_file_pages of that replica's D_REGROW_0128 checkpoint, or, for any H_REL checkpoint, differs from the actual_file_pages of that replica's P_ABS_16480 checkpoint, or in which the threshold or overshoot identities fail. P_ABS checkpoints carry target_baseline_pages null; D_GROW_0128 and D_REGROW_0128 keep their d_growth_observation baselines. No observation schema change is needed: the three fields already exist
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.rationale: a literal post-create capture would collapse the L ladder the plan's scientific design depends on. D_GROW_0128 is at least 128 pages above the post-create file and D_REGROW_0128 is at least 128 pages above D_RECREATE_EMPTY, which is not below D_GROW_0128 because the schedule never compacts the file, so the first L batch starts at least 256 pages above the post-create size: L_REL_0064 would already be satisfied by its first batch, the first polarity cross-check leg [D_REGROW_0128, L_REL_0064] and the first tdef_low_growth transition would carry one batch of growth instead of 64 pages, and every later L target would be reached about 256 pages early relative to the schedule the base plan inherited from A2 and declares not retuned. The H role would be distorted the same way by the roughly 16,000 pages of D, L, and P growth preceding it. The EXP-0042 design inputs that calibrate the legs (the leg-3 violation first at page 1021 between L_REL_0512 and L_REL_0768) were produced under the first-relative-batch capture, so preregistering that capture is what keeps A3 a prediction test on the same schedule rather than a retuned one
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.single_implementation: L baseline = actual_file_pages(D_REGROW_0128); H baseline = actual_file_pages(P_ABS_16480); disclosed per checkpoint and checked by both validators
relative_growth_baseline_reconciliation.worked_example: if D_REGROW_0128 closes at 301 pages, L_REL_0064 has threshold 365 and is captured at the first closed state of at least 365 pages, with target_baseline_pages 301; if P_ABS_16480 closes at 16,500 pages, H_REL_0064 has threshold 16,564 and target_baseline_pages 16,500

campaign_timeout_reconciliation.title: bounds.campaign_timeout_seconds is a hard evidence bound with a closed-bundle observable
campaign_timeout_reconciliation.plan_gap: bounds.campaign_timeout_seconds = 2700 is listed among the bounds and derived in runtime_design.campaign_headroom as the exact sum of the worker ceiling, the fan-in ceiling, and the setup and dispatch allowance, but no evidence document carries a campaign start or elapsed observable and no rule says who enforces it. PR #56 measures it from a clock started after checkout and setup and fails the fan-in job after the closed bundle has already been written with execution_status analysis_complete and campaign_failed false, so an over-time bundle can be retained under the successful-bundle identity and a detached consumer cannot tell
campaign_timeout_reconciliation.rule: campaign_timeout_seconds is a hard bound on retained evidence, not an advisory gate. Observable: the bundle manifest carries campaign_started_utc, the start time of the hosted workflow run attempt that produced the bundle as reported by the hosting service for that run id and attempt (the dispatch-side clock, which is the only observable that includes the setup and dispatch allowance; for GitHub Actions the run attempt's run_started_at), and campaign_elapsed_seconds, the whole number of seconds from campaign_started_utc to created_utc. The producer reads the campaign start before any evidence finalization, computes the elapsed time immediately before writing bundle-manifest.json, and writes execution_status analysis_complete only when campaign_elapsed_seconds is at most 2700; exactly 2700 is accepted and 2701 is rejected, per bounds_sanity_basis. If the bound is exceeded, or the campaign start cannot be read, the producer must not write a schema-valid bundle manifest and must not upload anything under the retained windows-dao-a3-bundle-<producer_commit>-<run_id>-<attempt> artifact name; the failure is recorded in the fan-in diagnostics artifact only, and the campaign is a failed campaign with no retained evidence. The producer validator and the independent validator reject a bundle whose manifest lacks either field, whose campaign_elapsed_seconds exceeds 2700, or whose campaign_elapsed_seconds differs from the floor of the difference between created_utc and campaign_started_utc. The independent validator cannot verify the truth of campaign_started_utc offline, exactly as it cannot verify created_utc; both are producer attestations bound to producer_commit, and the consistency and bound checks are what it recomputes
campaign_timeout_reconciliation.single_implementation: manifest fields campaign_started_utc and campaign_elapsed_seconds (0..2700); producer checks before writing the manifest; both validators recompute elapsed = floor(created_utc - campaign_started_utc) <= 2700
campaign_timeout_reconciliation.rationale: the base plan derives 2700 as a sum of ceilings, and bounds_sanity_basis requires every bound to be accepted at its ceiling and rejected one over; an advisory reading would leave the only bound in the table that no evidence document can witness. A hard bound can reject a scientifically sound run that was delayed by runner queueing; that costs one re-dispatch and loses no data, whereas an over-time bundle retained as successful evidence cannot be repaired afterwards. The per-replica and fan-in ceilings remain the job timeouts already bound by test
